text:
Consider that into smoke it turns,

the sweet good of your greatest contentment,

and human glory and the strongest pleasure

live scarcely one swift moment.


Such is man's immutable fate:

never to satisfy his anxious thought,

and at the price of his eagerness and torment

to acquire the rest of death.


Death, sad, pale, and divine,

awaits us at the end of our years

as the faithful wife awaits the unfaithful husband;


and by the ray of faith that lights her,

as austere as she appears to the wicked,

to the just man she presents herself beautiful.

translation.title: Consider That Into Smoke It Turns...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the moral sonnet's contrast between fleeting pleasure and death illuminated by faith.
